1664685496.title: \text{Engram of Layer 14}
1664685496.description: Engram is a memory. The model reads the memory by looking up short runs of text. An n-gram here is the run of the last two, three or four token identifiers that ends at a token. The three n-grams of each token are hashed into row numbers of a large learned table. The rows are read. The rows are projected into one key for each of the four residual streams and one value shared by the streams. Each stream is compared with its key. The comparison gives a gate g between zero and one. The value v times the gate is added to the stream. The module reads the token identifiers from the tape slot written by the input of the model. The module runs on the residual that enters layer 14. Layers 1 and 14 each hold a module with a table and weights of its own.

864211599.title: \text{Cast}
864211599.description: The cast reads a value held in BF16 and writes it in FP32. The written format holds an element in 32 bits against the 16 of the operand's format, and holds every number that format holds, so no value changes. 587508430.title: \text{Token Map}
587508430.description: Each token identifier is replaced by the identifier of its normalised text. The normalisation lowercases the text, removes accents and joins runs of white space. The tokens The, the and THE therefore receive one identifier. The n-grams that hold them address the same rows. The map is a lookup in a table M that has one entry for every token identifier and returns one of 99,092 compressed identifiers. The table is fixed. The released code builds it once from the tokenizer. Training never changes it.

2086738100.title: \text{Token Map}
2086738100.description: Replaces a token identifier by the identifier of the token's normalised text, so that tokens such as The, the and THE hash alike. The table M is fixed. The released code builds it once from the tokenizer. Training never changes it. The result of the table is a natural number below 99,092.

1491928810.title: ngram
1491928810.description: The view is the lookback of Engram. Slot i_L of token i_x reads the token i_L places before it. Slot 0 is therefore the token itself. The four slots hold the longest n-gram. A slot that reaches before the first token holds no value. The guarded axis L|x records which slots hold no value. The same view reads the compressed identifiers and the modality.

1537651249.title: \text{N-gram Hash}
1537651249.formula: \mathrm{hash}_{14}(c)[i_{G}, i_{K}] = \Big( \bigoplus_{i_{L} \in L,\; i_{L} \leq i_{G} + 1} \alpha_{14}[i_{L}]\, c[i_{L}] \Big) \bmod p_{14}[i_{G}, i_{K}] + o_{14}[i_{G}, i_{K}]
1537651249.description: An n-gram here is the run of the last two, three or four compressed identifiers that ends at a token. A table with one row for every possible n-gram would be too large, because 99,092 identifiers give about 10^20 different runs of four. Each n-gram is therefore hashed into one of about sixteen million rows per order and head. The hash is written out over integer operators. Each of the |L| identifiers is multiplied by the fixed odd multiplier of its slot. A multiplier is below 2^63 divided by the identifier bound, so every product is below 2^63 and is a 64-bit integer. The view named prefix reads, for each order, the products of the newest two, three or four slots. A slot not reached by the order holds the unit. The bitwise exclusive or of those products is one 64-bit integer per order. The exclusive or is defined on bit patterns, so the products carry a bound that is a power of two. The remainder of that integer after division by the prime of the order and the head is below that prime. The primes are one fixed array over the |G||K| pairs of an order and a head. The array holds the successive primes above 16,000,000 in the order the released layout draws them. The offset of a pair is the sum of the primes before it. The primes before a pair are read through the view named before and summed. The remainder plus the offset is therefore a row number in a range used by no other pair. The table has as many rows as the primes sum to. The primes and the offsets are then read over the orders and the heads. Two n-grams may share a row under one head and seldom share one under another, because the eight heads divide by eight different primes. The multipliers, the primes and the offsets belong to layer 14. The table addressed by that layer holds 384,016,682 rows, which is the sum of its 24 primes.

1388979204.title: p_{14}
1388979204.description: The primes of the hash of layer 14 are one for each of the |G||K| pairs of an n-gram order and a hash head, in the order the released layout draws them: the successive primes above the row count given by the configuration for one pair, sixteen million. The datatype of the array is the naturals below the bound p-bar, which is one bound standing over every prime of the layer, because a wire carries one datatype. A remainder after division by a prime is below that prime, so the same bound holds every remainder as well. The table of layer 14 has 384,016,682 rows, which is the sum of its primes. The offset of a pair is the sum of the primes before it. The row ranges of the pairs are therefore disjoint.

1730899721.title: \alpha_{14}
1730899721.description: The multipliers of the hash of layer 14 are one odd integer per lookback slot. They are drawn once for that layer from a random number generator seeded by the layer, so the two Engram layers hash differently. An identifier is below the identifier bound. A multiplier is below 2^63 divided by that bound. The product of the two is therefore below 2^63 and is a 64-bit integer with nothing cast.

996062443.title: prefix
996062443.description: The view is the prefix of the lookback slots read by each n-gram order. The order i_G reads the slot i_L' + i_G + 1 - |G| of the products. The order therefore covers the newest i_G + 2 slots. The slots not reached by the order hold no value. The exclusive or that follows ignores those slots, so one reduction gives the hash of the 2-gram, the 3-gram and the 4-gram.

156994982.title: pair
156994982.description: The view reads an array over the |G||K| pairs as an array over the n-gram orders and the hash heads. The pair |K| i_G + i_K stands at the order i_G and the head i_K. The released layout draws the primes in that order. The primes and the offsets are both read this way.

1162670009.title: before
1162670009.description: The view reads the primes that stand before each pair of an n-gram order and a hash head. The pair i_GK reads the prime at i_GK' + i_GK - |GK|. The primes before the pair therefore fill the last i_GK slots. The earlier slots hold no value. The sum over the slots is the offset of the pair. The rows of that pair begin at the offset in the table.

259034755.title: pair
259034755.description: The view reads an array over the |G||K| pairs as an array over the n-gram orders and the hash heads. The pair |K| i_G + i_K stands at the order i_G and the head i_K. The released layout draws the primes in that order. The primes and the offsets are both read this way.

1343646802.title: \mathrm{cast}
1343646802.description: Pyncd represents Natural values as a bounded datatype. Here the cast names the correct size for the subsequent embedding, which uses the bound to determine its size. The value read and the value written are both held in INT64.

469839001.title: \text{N-gram Table}
469839001.description: Each of the 24 row numbers of a token, one for every n-gram order and hash head, is looked up in the learned table of this layer, which gives 24 vectors of width |D| = 256. One linear map reads the 24 vectors together and gives one key for each residual stream. A second map gives one value shared by every stream. The released code holds the two maps as one weight and cuts its result in two. The table of layer 14 has 384,016,682 rows, which is the sum of the 24 primes of the layer. The released code stores the rows in FP8 with one scale for every 32 channels and converts a row to reals when the row is read.

2042052174.title: \text{N-gram Table}
2042052174.description: Returns the learned row of width 256 named by a row number, from the n-gram table of layer 14, which holds 384,016,682 rows. One token looks up 24 rows, one for every n-gram order and hash head. The released code stores the rows in FP8 with one scale for every 32 channels and converts a row to reals when the row is read.

1348850376.title: \text{Engram Gate}
1348850376.formula: y[i_{x}, i_{n}] = \frac{\sum_{i_{m} \in m} X[i_{x}, i_{n}, i_{m}]\, w[i_{n}, i_{m}]\, k[i_{x}, i_{n}, i_{m}]}{\mathrm{rms}(X[i_{x}, i_{n}])\, \mathrm{rms}(k[i_{x}, i_{n}])}, \quad g[i_{x}, i_{n}] = \sigma\Big( \mathrm{sign}(y) \sqrt{\max(\lvert y \rvert \lvert m \rvert^{-1/2}, \varepsilon_{\mathrm{g}})} \Big)
1348850376.description: A stream receives the looked-up value multiplied by its gate. Each stream of a token is multiplied channel by channel with its key and with a learned weight. The products are summed over the channels. The sum is divided by the root mean square of the stream, by the root mean square of the key and by the square root of the width. Multiplying the stream or the key by a positive constant therefore leaves the result unchanged. The two root mean squares have an epsilon under the root and no learned gain. The gate is the sigmoid of the signed square root of that number. The gate is above one half where the sum is positive and below one half where the sum is negative. The released code multiplies the gate by one minus the modality of the token. The multiplication sets the gate to zero at an image token. A model that reads text alone holds no image token.

1443128907.title: \text{Cast}
1443128907.description: The cast reads a value held in BF16 and writes it in FP32. The written format holds an element in 32 bits against the 16 of the operand's format, and holds every number that format holds, so no value changes. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

322008153.title: \text{Cast}
322008153.description: The cast reads a value held in BF16 and writes it in FP32. The written format holds an element in 32 bits against the 16 of the operand's format, and holds every number that format holds, so no value changes. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

137670381.title: \mathrm{gate}
137670381.description: This map is the gate of the Engram module. The normalised dot product of a stream with its key is divided by the square root of the width. The magnitude of that product is kept at or above one millionth. The square root of the magnitude is taken. The sign of the dot product is put back. A sigmoid follows. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

1598645706.title: \text{Third Encoder Group}
1598645706.description: The third encoder group, which is layers 14 to 19: a Full layer followed by five Reuse layers, as in the two groups before it. The group is drawn on its own because Engram is applied to the residual before layer 14, which is the first layer of this group. A step that runs before the third group and before no other group cannot stand inside a block that repeats the same body three times, so the third group cannot be an iteration of that block. The two groups before it write the members 0 and 1 of the entries and of the selection, one member per iteration. This group writes and reads member 2, which is named by the constant 2 because no counter runs here.

1713758829.title: \text{Single-Pass mHC}
1713758829.description: One sublayer runs inside the four-stream residual. The coefficients are predicted from the four streams. The streams are summed into one hidden state under the collapse vector predicted by the previous sublayer. The hidden state is normalised. The body runs on the result. The output vector times the body's result is added to the combine matrix applied to the four streams. The collapse vector predicted here goes to the next sublayer.

775378740.title: \text{Cast}
775378740.description: The cast reads a value held in BF16 and writes it in FP32. 921044640.title: \sigma
921044640.description: The sigmoid is applied to the collapse vector of a hyper-connection, so the weight of each stream lies between zero and one. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

27423970.title: x + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{hc}}
27423970.description: This map adds the epsilon of the hyper-connections, `hc_eps` in the released configuration, which is one millionth. The epsilon is added to the collapse vector after the sigmoid and to the combine matrix after the row softmax. Every value is therefore above zero. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

2137773455.title: 2\sigma
2137773455.description: Twice the sigmoid is applied to the output vector of a hyper-connection, so the weight of each stream lies between zero and two. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1749827460.title: x + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{hc}}

1798063302.title: \text{Full Attention}
1798063302.description: The Full layer of an encoder group compresses every two consecutive tokens of its hidden state into one entry and makes one indexer key from each entry. The layer rotates and rounds both as the released caches hold them. The query and the window latents are rotated by the positions of their tokens. The window latents are then rounded to the eight-bit FP8 format, as the released window cache holds them. The layer scores every entry reached by each query and keeps the 512 best. The layer then attends over the window and the kept entries under one softmax. The scores are multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width before the softmax. The result of the attention is rotated back by the position of its query before the output projection. The entries and the selection are stored on the tape, which holds what one layer leaves for another. The Reuse layers of the same group read the entries and the selection there.

226090859.title: \text{Cast to MXFP8}
226090859.formula: \begin{gathered}a[i_{g}] = \max_{i_{y} \in y} \lvert x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] \rvert \\s[i_{g}] = 2^{\lceil \log_{2} (\max(a[i_{g}],\, 10^{-4}) / 448) \rceil} \\\hat{x}[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] = \mathrm{E4M3}\big(\ulcorner x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] / s[i_{g}] \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}\big)\end{gathered}
226090859.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

917950499.description: Reads every two adjacent channels as one complex number, with the first channel as the real part and the second as the imaginary part. A complex number is a point in a plane. Multiplying the point by a complex number of length one turns it about the origin, so the rotation of a pair is one product.

1287846723.formula: y[2 i_{t}] = \mathrm{Re}\, p[i_{t}], \qquad y[2 i_{t} + 1] = \mathrm{Im}\, p[i_{t}]

506229411.description: The magnitude of a channel is the channel without its sign. The largest magnitude of a group sets the scale of the group. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1953328844.title: \max(x, 10^{-4})
1953328844.description: Keeps the largest magnitude of a group at or above 10^-4, so a group of zeros is not divided by zero. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

868598548.title: x / 448
868598548.description: This map divides the largest magnitude of a group by 448, the largest number held by the E4M3 form. A group divided by this scale has its largest channel at 448. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1119382472.title: \log_{2} x
1119382472.description: This map takes the logarithm to base two of the scale. The ceiling of this number is the exponent of the smallest power of two at or above the scale. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

92568779.title: \text{Ceiling}
92568779.formula: \lceil \cdot \rceil : R[\,] \to R[\,], \qquad \lceil x \rceil = \min \{ n \in \mathbb{Z} : n \geq x \}
92568779.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest whole number. Here the number is the logarithm to base two of a scale, so two to the power of the result is the smallest power of two at or above the scale. The released kernel reads the exponent bits of the scale and adds one where any mantissa bit is set. The package has no numeric for a ceiling or a floor, so this step is a generic operator.

5283799.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}
5283799.description: Keeps a divided channel between -448 and 448, the range of the E4M3 form. The scale is rounded up, so every channel is already inside the range. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

410327429.title: \text{Cast to E4M3}

The largest number is 448 and the smallest above zero is 2^-9. The operator names the datatype read and the datatype returned. The package writes no formula for the rounding.

37856922.title: \text{Cast from E4M3}
37856922.description: Reads each E4M3 number as a real. No value changes. The operations that follow are computed in reals, as the released kernel computes them in 32-bit floats.

1315165418.title: qgrp
1315165418.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

1716141800.description: The view is the sliding window. Slot i_w of query i_x reads the token i_w places before the query. A slot that reaches before the first token holds no value. The guarded axis w|x records which slots hold no value.

2092775892.title: \text{Compressor}
2092775892.description: In the ratio-2 compressor two consecutive tokens form one entry. Each token is projected to a value and to a gate. A softmax over the two tokens of each channel weights the values. The weighted sum is normalised.

377751023.title: grp
377751023.description: Cuts one axis into consecutive groups of equal size, so a position of the result is a group and a place inside it. The attention cuts the heads into groups for the grouped output projection. The ratio-2 compressor cuts the tokens into entries of two. The pixel unshuffle of the image pathway cuts the rows of the patch grid into cell rows of three and its columns into cell columns of three.

1093900685.title: \text{Cast}
1093900685.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

1423445455.title: \text{Cast to MXFP8}
1423445455.formula: \begin{gathered}a[i_{g}] = \max_{i_{y} \in y} \lvert x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] \rvert \\s[i_{g}] = 2^{\lceil \log_{2} (\max(a[i_{g}],\, 10^{-4}) / 448) \rceil} \\\hat{x}[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] = \mathrm{E4M3}\big(\ulcorner x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] / s[i_{g}] \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}\big)\end{gathered}
1423445455.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

1298483791.title: \text{Pairs as Complex Numbers}

Multiplying the point by a complex number of length one turns it about the origin, so the rotation of a pair is one product.

1619519402.title: \text{Cast}

1972337319.title: x / 6

1806934416.title: \log_{2} x

1068618749.title: \text{Ceiling}

The released kernel reads the exponent bits of the scale and adds one where any mantissa bit is set. The package has no numeric for a ceiling or a floor, so this step is a generic operator.

1146206721.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-6}^{6}

568884023.title: \text{Attention Core}

Every score is multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model, before it is exponentiated. The scale keeps the spread of the scores the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The sink logit is one learned number per head that lets the head give part of its weight to no slot. The sink logit is exponentiated with no scale.

625415320.title: \lvert c \rvert^{-1/2} x
625415320.description: This map multiplies every attention score by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model. A score is a sum over the 512 channels of a latent, so its spread grows with the square root of that width. The scale keeps the spread the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The model drawn without the omitted mechanisms folds this factor into the query weight. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1178136612.title: z^{-1}

The division is written as a product with this reciprocal. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1845328088.title: \text{Single-Pass mHC}
1845328088.description: One sublayer runs inside the four-stream residual. The coefficients are predicted from the four streams. The result rides a sparse axis, labelled with the count kept and the axis selected over, which holds that many live positions. No index is therefore handed out beside the scores.

446885226.title: \text{Select}

1518020092.title: \tfrac{3}{2}x

401552601.title: \text{Reuse Layer}
401552601.description: One of the five Reuse layers of the third encoder group: a Reuse attention sublayer reading member 2 of the entries and of the selection, written by the Full layer of the third group, and a mixture sublayer, each inside the four-stream residual.

287243756.title: \text{Single-Pass mHC}
287243756.description: One sublayer runs inside the four-stream residual. The coefficients are predicted from the four streams. The streams are summed into one hidden state under the collapse vector predicted by the previous sublayer. The hidden state is normalised. The body runs on the result. 415189475.title: \text{Reuse Attention}
415189475.description: A Reuse layer reads the entries and the selection from the tape, which holds what an earlier layer left for it. The layer therefore compresses no tokens and scores no entries. The window latents are then rounded to the eight-bit FP8 format, as the released window cache holds them. The layer reads the latents of the selected entries and attends over the window and those entries under one softmax. The scores are multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width before the softmax. The result of the attention is rotated back by the position of its query before the output projection.

162876609.title: qgrp
162876609.description: Cuts the channels of one latent into consecutive groups of equal size. Channel i_y of group i_E reads channel |y| i_E + i_y of the latent. Every group is rounded with a scale of its own, so one large channel reduces the precision of its own group and of no other group.

1522390160.title: \lvert x \rvert
1522390160.description: The magnitude of a channel is the channel without its sign. The largest magnitude of a group sets the scale of the group. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

146493048.title: \max(x, 10^{-4})
146493048.description: Keeps the largest magnitude of a group at or above 10^-4, so a group of zeros is not divided by zero. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

313986405.title: x / 448
313986405.description: This map divides the largest magnitude of a group by 448, the largest number held by the E4M3 form. A group divided by this scale has its largest channel at 448. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1547640541.title: \log_{2} x
1547640541.description: This map takes the logarithm to base two of the scale. The ceiling of this number is the exponent of the smallest power of two at or above the scale. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

976790332.title: \text{Ceiling}
976790332.formula: \lceil \cdot \rceil : R[\,] \to R[\,], \qquad \lceil x \rceil = \min \{ n \in \mathbb{Z} : n \geq x \}
976790332.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest whole number. Here the number is the logarithm to base two of a scale, so two to the power of the result is the smallest power of two at or above the scale. The released kernel reads the exponent bits of the scale and adds one where any mantissa bit is set. The package has no numeric for a ceiling or a floor, so this step is a generic operator.

56785314.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}
56785314.description: Keeps a divided channel between -448 and 448, the range of the E4M3 form. The scale is rounded up, so every channel is already inside the range. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

77017559.title: \text{Cast to E4M3}
77017559.description: Rounds each value to the nearest number held by the E4M3 form. The form has eight bits: a sign, four exponent bits and three mantissa bits. The largest number is 448 and the smallest above zero is 2^-9. The operator names the datatype read and the datatype returned. The package writes no formula for the rounding.

426824768.title: \text{Cast from E4M3}
426824768.description: Reads each E4M3 number as a real. No value changes. The operations that follow are computed in reals, as the released kernel computes them in 32-bit floats.

194582338.title: qgrp
194582338.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

83766707.title: \text{Cast}
83766707.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. The written format holds an element in 16 bits against the 32 of the operand's format, so every value is replaced by the nearest number the written format holds. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

480402141.title: win
480402141.description: The view is the sliding window. Slot i_w of query i_x reads the token i_w places before the query. A slot that reaches before the first token holds no value. The guarded axis w|x records which slots hold no value.

1213939107.title: \text{Entry Gather}
1213939107.description: The gather reads the latents of the selected entries. The compressed entries are read back from every entry and merged onto the queries the way the indexer reads its keys. One latent is read per slot at the distance held by the selection for that slot.

167796901.title: back
167796901.description: Counts entries back from the entry named by a position. Distance i_r of entry i_b reads the entry i_r places before it. A distance that reaches before the first entry holds no value.

1257613507.title: pos
1257613507.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. The input does not carry every axis read by the row, so one copy of the input is written for every position of the missing axes. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

720550004.title: \text{IndexSelect}
720550004.description: Reads the payload at an index that arrives as data. The index is a natural number below the size of the axis it reads along. The operator is broadcast over every other axis, so one entry is read per index.

863587059.title: \text{Concatenation}
863587059.description: Writes each input onto its own run of the concatenated axis. The second run comes after the first. The size of that axis is therefore the sum of the sizes of the parts. Every other axis is carried through unchanged.

658869866.title: \text{Attention Core}
658869866.description: The attention core computes one head's softmax over the window slots, the selected entries and the learned sink. The two kinds of latent are laid end to end along one slot axis. The query scores against the latent at every slot. The scores are exponentiated. One copy is summed into the denominator together with the exponentiated sink logit. The reciprocal of that sum scales the exponentials contracted against the latents. Every score is multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model, before it is exponentiated. The scale keeps the spread of the scores the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The sink logit is one learned number per head that lets the head give part of its weight to no slot. The sink logit is exponentiated with no scale.

376335738.title: \lvert c \rvert^{-1/2} x
376335738.description: This map multiplies every attention score by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model. A score is a sum over the 512 channels of a latent, so its spread grows with the square root of that width. The scale keeps the spread the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The model drawn without the omitted mechanisms folds this factor into the query weight. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1735617423.title: z^{-1}
1735617423.description: This map is the reciprocal of a normalising sum. The attention core divides each exponentiated score by the sum over its slots and the sink. The division is written as a product with this reciprocal. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1269844291.title: \text{Full Attention}
1269844291.description: The Full layer of the decoder projects each token of its hidden state into one entry and makes one indexer key from each entry. The layer rotates and rounds both as the released caches hold them. The query and the window latents are rotated by the positions of their tokens. The window latents are then rounded to the eight-bit FP8 format, as the released window cache holds them. The layer scores every entry reached by each query and keeps the 512 best. The layer then attends over the window and the kept entries under one softmax. The scores are multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width before the softmax. The result of the attention is rotated back by the position of its query before the output projection. The layer also keeps the 2048 best blocks of eight entries as the candidate pool. The newest block is always among them. The layer stores the entries, the keys, the pool and the selection on the tape, which holds them for every later decoder layer.

487234427.title: \text{Concatenation of the Channels}

1257865852.title: qgrp

1668330316.title: \lvert x \rvert

1108060506.title: \max(x, 10^{-4})

939508304.title: x / 448

159566533.title: \log_{2} x

1994133402.title: \text{Ceiling}

853891537.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}

352677900.formula: \begin{gathered} y[i_{B}, |\bar{d}| + 2 i_{t}] + \mathrm{i}\, y[i_{B}, |\bar{d}| + 2 i_{t} + 1] = F[i_{B}, i_{t}]\, \big(v[i_{B}, |\bar{d}| + 2 i_{t}] + \mathrm{i}\, v[i_{B}, |\bar{d}| + 2 i_{t} + 1]\big) \\ y[i_{B}, i_{\bar{d}}] = v[i_{B}, i_{\bar{d}}] \end{gathered}
352677900.description: Each indexer key of the decoder is made from one compressed entry, which stands for one token. The key is rotated by the position of that token. The circle in the box is the table of turns, which holds one turn for every position and every pair of channels.

1533904032.title: \text{Lightning Indexer}
1533904032.description: The lightning indexer scores every compressed entry reached by a query, so that the attention reads the best-scoring entries alone. The shared indexer keys arrive rotated and rounded. The keys are read back from every entry and merged onto the queries, so each query holds the keys of the entries reached by that query. The released code is a reference implementation. It keeps the rounded keys and queries as 16-bit numbers and scores in 16-bit, so it takes neither the smaller cache nor the faster scoring.

1320417521.formula: \begin{gathered}a[i_{g}] = \max_{i_{y} \in y} \lvert x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] \rvert \\s[i_{g}] = 2^{\lceil \log_{2} (\max(a[i_{g}],\, 10^{-4}) / 448) \rceil} \\\hat{x}[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] = \mathrm{E4M3}\big(\ulcorner x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] / s[i_{g}] \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}\big)\end{gathered}
1320417521.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

1211314350.title: \text{Indexer Scores}
1211314350.description: One query is scored against every compressed entry reached by the query. The entries read by the attention are chosen from the scores. Each of the 32 indexer heads takes the product of its rotated and rounded indexer query with the key of the entry. A negative product is set to zero. The 32 results are summed under one weight per head, which is read off the hidden state of the token. The weights are multiplied by one over the square root of the key width times the head count, which is 1/64 in the released model. The released code computes the product with an ordinary 16-bit multiply over keys and queries that were rounded to four bits and written back as 16-bit numbers. The score is therefore the one given by a four-bit multiply. The reference implementation takes neither the smaller key cache nor the faster scoring.

145379970.title: (\lvert d \rvert \lvert i \rvert)^{-1/2} x
145379970.description: This map multiplies the weight of every indexer head by 1/64. The released indexer multiplies by one over the square root of the key width, which is 128, and by one over the square root of the head count, which is 32. The model drawn without the omitted mechanisms folds this factor into the weight `w^{I}`. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1516057274.title: \text{TopK}
1516057274.formula: \{p[i_{s|x}]\} = \{i_{r|x} : s[i_{r|x}] \text{ is among the } |s|_{512} \text{ largest of } s\}
1516057274.description: Keeps the positions of the largest scores along the axis consumed and hands out no score, because nothing reads a score after the selection. Each result is a natural number, one per slot of the result's axis. A slot with no entry to hold reads the unit.

2046904689.title: \text{Candidate Pool}
2046904689.description: The block turns one token's indexer scores into the distances each Reindex layer scores inside. The distances are split into blocks of eight. Each block keeps its best score. The block of the eight newest entries is pinned. The 2048 best blocks are kept. The eight distances of every kept block are laid out along the candidate axis.

25360192.title: blk
25360192.description: Cuts the distances reached by a query into blocks of |u| consecutive distances. Offset i_u of block i_P reads distance |u| i_P + i_u. The candidate pool keeps the best score of each block.

2136810350.title: \text{Pinned Newest Block}
2136810350.formula: \mathrm{pin}(b)[i_{P}] = b[i_{P}] + J[i_{P}], \qquad J[0] = \infty, \qquad J[i_{P}] = 0 \text{ for } i_{P} \neq 0
2136810350.description: The block of the eight newest entries is always kept as a candidate. Positive infinity is written at block 0 and added to the block scores. Every other block keeps its score. No score is larger than infinity, so the Top-2048 that follows keeps block 0. The released code numbers its blocks by absolute entry. The newest block of the released code is still filling and holds between one and eight entries, so an older block that is full could score higher. The released code pins the newest block so that a full older block cannot displace it. The model drawn here numbers the blocks by distance back from the newest entry reached by a query, so block 0 holds the newest entries of every query. Once a query has reached eight entries, block 0 holds eight of them. Every entry pinned by the released code is therefore in block 0, beside up to seven older entries.

6753942.title: \text{Positive Infinity}
6753942.description: Positive infinity is larger than every score. Written at block 0 and added to the block scores of a query, it puts the block of the newest entries ahead of every other block, so the Top-2048 over the blocks keeps that block.

The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

667637885.title: \text{Concatenation of the Channels}
667637885.description: Joins the channels left alone by the rotation and the rotated channels back into one vector. The run left alone comes first and the rotated run comes after it. The result has the channel axis the vector arrived on, so an operation that reads the vector reads the same axis whether or not the vector was rotated.

1211425214.title: qgrp
1211425214.description: Cuts the channels of one latent into consecutive groups of equal size. Channel i_y of group i_E reads channel |y| i_E + i_y of the latent. Every group is rounded with a scale of its own, so one large channel reduces the precision of its own group and of no other group.

410814290.title: \text{Cast}
410814290.description: The cast reads a value held in BF16 and writes it in FP32. The written format holds an element in 32 bits against the 16 of the operand's format, and holds every number that format holds, so no value changes. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

2064887143.title: \lvert x \rvert
2064887143.description: The magnitude of a channel is the channel without its sign. The largest magnitude of a group sets the scale of the group. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

775724172.title: x / 6
775724172.description: This map divides the largest magnitude of a group by 6, the largest number held by the E2M1 form. A group divided by this scale has its largest channel at 6. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

605126266.title: \max(x, 2^{-9})
605126266.description: Keeps the scale of a group at or above 2^-9, the smallest number above zero held by the E4M3 form, so a group of zeros is not divided by zero. The released kernel keeps the largest magnitude at or above 6 times 2^-9 before it divides by 6, which is the same function. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

287793033.title: \text{Cast to E4M3}
287793033.description: Rounds each value to the nearest number held by the E4M3 form. The form has eight bits: a sign, four exponent bits and three mantissa bits. The largest number is 448 and the smallest above zero is 2^-9. The operator names the datatype read and the datatype returned. The package writes no formula for the rounding.

1882793586.title: \text{Cast from E4M3}
1882793586.description: Reads each E4M3 number as a real. No value changes. The operations that follow are computed in reals, as the released kernel computes them in 32-bit floats.

1894024681.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-6}^{6}
1894024681.description: Keeps a divided channel between -6 and 6, the range of the E2M1 form. A scale rounded up to a power of two leaves every channel inside the range. A scale rounded through E4M3 can round down. The clamp then holds the largest channel at 6. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1487813033.title: \text{Cast to E2M1}
1487813033.description: Rounds each value to the nearest number held by the E2M1 form. The form has four bits: a sign, two exponent bits and one mantissa bit. The numbers are 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4 and 6 with either sign. The operator names the datatype read and the datatype returned. The package writes no formula for the rounding.

1737883441.title: \text{Cast from E2M1}
1737883441.description: Reads each E2M1 number as a real. No value changes. The operations that follow are computed in reals, as the released kernel computes them in 32-bit floats.

1052263186.title: qgrp
1052263186.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

1918567144.title: \text{Cast}
1918567144.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. The written format holds an element in 16 bits against the 32 of the operand's format, so every value is replaced by the nearest number the written format holds. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

728312760.title: \text{Entry Gather}
728312760.description: The gather reads the latents of the selected entries. The compressed entries are read back from every entry and merged onto the queries the way the indexer reads its keys. One latent is read per slot at the distance held by the selection for that slot.

446784898.title: back
446784898.description: Counts entries back from the entry named by a position. Distance i_r of entry i_b reads the entry i_r places before it. A distance that reaches before the first entry holds no value.

2036767791.title: pos
2036767791.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

1077786797.title: \text{IndexSelect}
1077786797.description: Reads the payload at an index that arrives as data. The index is a natural number below the size of the axis it reads along. The operator is broadcast over every other axis, so one entry is read per index.

444426079.title: \text{Concatenation}
444426079.description: Writes each input onto its own run of the concatenated axis. The second run comes after the first. The size of that axis is therefore the sum of the sizes of the parts. Every other axis is carried through unchanged.

671103403.title: \text{Attention Core}
671103403.description: The attention core computes one head's softmax over the window slots, the selected entries and the learned sink. The two kinds of latent are laid end to end along one slot axis. The query scores against the latent at every slot. The scores are exponentiated. One copy is summed into the denominator together with the exponentiated sink logit. The reciprocal of that sum scales the exponentials contracted against the latents. Every score is multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model, before it is exponentiated. The scale keeps the spread of the scores the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The sink logit is one learned number per head that lets the head give part of its weight to no slot. The sink logit is exponentiated with no scale.

1555881844.title: \lvert c \rvert^{-1/2} x
1555881844.description: This map multiplies every attention score by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model. A score is a sum over the 512 channels of a latent, so its spread grows with the square root of that width. The scale keeps the spread the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The model drawn without the omitted mechanisms folds this factor into the query weight. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1684233870.title: z^{-1}
1684233870.description: This map is the reciprocal of a normalising sum. The attention core divides each exponentiated score by the sum over its slots and the sink. The division is written as a product with this reciprocal. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

2146341021.title: \text{Cast}

1042571780.title: \text{Pairs as Complex Numbers}
1042571780.description: Reads every two adjacent channels as one complex number, with the first channel as the real part and the second as the imaginary part. A complex number is a point in a plane. Multiplying the point by a complex number of length one turns it about the origin, so the rotation of a pair is one product.

2062922154.title: \text{Cast}
2062922154.description: The cast reads a value held in BF16 and writes it in FP32. The written format holds an element in 32 bits against the 16 of the operand's format, and holds every number that format holds, so no value changes. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

2140707380.title: \text{Complex Numbers as Pairs}
2140707380.formula: y[2 i_{t}] = \mathrm{Re}\, p[i_{t}], \qquad y[2 i_{t} + 1] = \mathrm{Im}\, p[i_{t}]
2140707380.description: Writes every complex number back as two adjacent channels, with the real part first and the imaginary part second. The operation undoes the reading of the channels as pairs.

1740084663.title: \text{Cast}

1010989394.title: grp

157057718.title: \text{Cast to MXFP8}

157057718.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

1046191607.title: \text{Single-Pass mHC}

The streams are summed into one hidden state under the collapse vector predicted by the previous sublayer. The hidden state is normalised. The body runs on the result. The output vector times the body's result is added to the combine matrix applied to the four streams. The collapse vector predicted here goes to the next sublayer.

1917811323.title: \sigma
1917811323.description: The sigmoid is applied to the collapse vector of a hyper-connection, so the weight of each stream lies between zero and one. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

494315806.title: x + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{hc}}
494315806.description: This map adds the epsilon of the hyper-connections, `hc_eps` in the released configuration, which is one millionth. The epsilon is added to the collapse vector after the sigmoid and to the combine matrix after the row softmax. Every value is therefore above zero. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1716946620.title: 2\sigma
1716946620.description: Twice the sigmoid is applied to the output vector of a hyper-connection, so the weight of each stream lies between zero and two. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

The released configuration sets none, so the released value is one. A larger temperature would bring the scores of the experts closer together. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

The square root of the positive score is taken. The result is the gate of the expert. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

820013185.title: \text{TopK}
820013185.formula: y[i_{e}] = s[i_{e}] \text{ where } s[i_{e}] \text{ is among the } |k|_{6} \text{ largest of } s

The layer reads the latents of the selected entries and attends over the window and those entries under one softmax. 2056111193.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

379081224.title: \max(x, 10^{-4})

432022477.title: x / 448

560274701.title: \log_{2} x
560274701.description: This map takes the logarithm to base two of the scale. The ceiling of this number is the exponent of the smallest power of two at or above the scale. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1735426460.title: \text{Ceiling}
1735426460.formula: \lceil \cdot \rceil : R[\,] \to R[\,], \qquad \lceil x \rceil = \min \{ n \in \mathbb{Z} : n \geq x \}
1735426460.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest whole number. Here the number is the logarithm to base two of a scale, so two to the power of the result is the smallest power of two at or above the scale. The released kernel reads the exponent bits of the scale and adds one where any mantissa bit is set. The package has no numeric for a ceiling or a floor, so this step is a generic operator.

298531400.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}

764590052.title: \text{Cast to E4M3}

1348836731.title: \text{Cast from E4M3}
1348836731.description: Reads each E4M3 number as a real. No value changes. The operations that follow are computed in reals, as the released kernel computes them in 32-bit floats.

2060908055.title: qgrp
2060908055.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

665603039.title: win

1201548377.title: \text{Entry Gather}
1201548377.description: The gather reads the latents of the selected entries. The compressed entries are read back from every entry and merged onto the queries the way the indexer reads its keys. One latent is read per slot at the distance held by the selection for that slot.

897102642.title: back
897102642.description: Counts entries back from the entry named by a position. Distance i_r of entry i_b reads the entry i_r places before it. A distance that reaches before the first entry holds no value.

1309322278.title: pos
1309322278.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

1563065808.title: \text{IndexSelect}

718607891.title: \text{Concatenation}

678113622.title: \text{Attention Core}

One copy is summed into the denominator together with the exponentiated sink logit. The reciprocal of that sum scales the exponentials contracted against the latents. Every score is multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model, before it is exponentiated. The scale keeps the spread the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The model drawn without the omitted mechanisms folds this factor into the query weight. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1502941183.title: z^{-1}

898026098.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-\lambda}^{\lambda}

Every other value is kept. The limit is 10 in the released configuration and comes from training, where it keeps the activations inside the range represented by the FP8 and FP4 number formats. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1300247603.title: \text{Cast}
1300247603.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. The written format holds an element in 16 bits against the 32 of the operand's format, so every value is replaced by the nearest number the written format holds. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

822087610.title: \text{Cast to MXFP8}
822087610.formula: \begin{gathered}a[i_{g}] = \max_{i_{y} \in y} \lvert x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] \rvert \\s[i_{g}] = 2^{\lceil \log_{2} (\max(a[i_{g}],\, 10^{-4}) / 448) \rceil} \\\hat{x}[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] = \mathrm{E4M3}\big(\ulcorner x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] / s[i_{g}] \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}\big)\end{gathered}
822087610.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

772823819.title: \text{Reindex Group}
772823819.description: One of the four Reindex groups of the decoder, which are layers 24 to 39: a Reindex layer that scores inside the candidate pool and writes a fresh selection, followed by three Reuse layers that read it. Each iteration writes and reads the member of the selection named by the group counter l. The multimodal model writes the fourth group on its own, because DSpark reads the residual that enters each of its three Reuse layers. This model has no DSpark to read that residual.

474213553.title: \text{Single-Pass mHC}
474213553.description: One sublayer runs inside the four-stream residual. The coefficients are predicted from the four streams. The streams are summed into one hidden state under the collapse vector predicted by the previous sublayer. The hidden state is normalised. The body runs on the result. The output vector times the body's result is added to the combine matrix applied to the four streams. The collapse vector predicted here goes to the next sublayer.

1794402573.title: x + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{hc}}

The epsilon is added to the collapse vector after the sigmoid and to the combine matrix after the row softmax. Every value is therefore above zero. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

649967521.title: 2\sigma

951196658.title: \text{Reindex Attention}
951196658.description: A Reindex layer reads the entries, the indexer keys and the candidate pool from the tape, which holds what the Full layer of the decoder left for later layers. All three arrive rotated and rounded. The query and the window latents are rotated by the positions of their tokens. The window latents are then rounded to the eight-bit FP8 format, as the released window cache holds them. The layer scores its own rotated and rounded indexer queries against the entries of the pool alone and keeps the 512 best. The layer then attends over the window and the kept entries under one softmax. The scores are multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width before the softmax. The result of the attention is rotated back by the position of its query before the output projection. The new selection is stored on the tape, where the Reuse layers of the same group read it.

1853594005.title: \log_{2} x
1853594005.description: This map takes the logarithm to base two of the scale. The ceiling of this number is the exponent of the smallest power of two at or above the scale. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1911083258.title: \text{Ceiling}
1911083258.formula: \lceil \cdot \rceil : R[\,] \to R[\,], \qquad \lceil x \rceil = \min \{ n \in \mathbb{Z} : n \geq x \}
1911083258.description: Rounds a number up to the nearest whole number. Here the number is the logarithm to base two of a scale, so two to the power of the result is the smallest power of two at or above the scale. The released kernel reads the exponent bits of the scale and adds one where any mantissa bit is set. The package has no numeric for a ceiling or a floor, so this step is a generic operator.

431910632.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}

884192997.title: \text{Cast to E4M3}
884192997.description: Rounds each value to the nearest number held by the E4M3 form. The form has eight bits: a sign, four exponent bits and three mantissa bits. The largest number is 448 and the smallest above zero is 2^-9. The operator names the datatype read and the datatype returned. The package writes no formula for the rounding.

2109232441.title: \text{Cast from E4M3}
2109232441.description: Reads each E4M3 number as a real. No value changes. The operations that follow are computed in reals, as the released kernel computes them in 32-bit floats.

1344906263.title: qgrp
1344906263.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

517235797.title: win
517235797.description: The view is the sliding window. Slot i_w of query i_x reads the token i_w places before the query. A slot that reaches before the first token holds no value. The guarded axis w|x records which slots hold no value.

129008273.title: \text{Lightning Indexer}
129008273.description: The lightning indexer scores every compressed entry reached by a query, so that the attention reads the best-scoring entries alone. The indexer query of every head is projected from the low-rank query latent, rotated by the position of its token and rounded to the four-bit FP4 format. The shared indexer keys arrive rotated and rounded. The keys are read back from every entry and merged onto the queries, so each query holds the keys of the entries reached by that query. The scoring box scores one query against those keys. The rounding makes the scores equal those of a system that keeps the keys as four-bit numbers and scores them on the four-bit hardware path. The released code is a reference implementation. It keeps the rounded keys and queries as 16-bit numbers and scores in 16-bit, so it takes neither the smaller cache nor the faster scoring.

The released kernel reads the exponent bits of the scale and adds one where any mantissa bit is set. The package has no numeric for a ceiling or a floor, so this step is a generic operator.

1378817077.title: \ulcorner x \lrcorner_{-6}^{6}
1378817077.description: Keeps a divided channel between -6 and 6, the range of the E2M1 form. A scale rounded up to a power of two leaves every channel inside the range. A scale rounded through E4M3 can round down. The clamp then holds the largest channel at 6. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1314606407.title: \text{Cast to E2M1}
1314606407.description: Rounds each value to the nearest number held by the E2M1 form. The form has four bits: a sign, two exponent bits and one mantissa bit. The numbers are 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4 and 6 with either sign. The operator names the datatype read and the datatype returned. The package writes no formula for the rounding.

1778426097.title: \text{Cast from E2M1}
1778426097.description: Reads each E2M1 number as a real. No value changes. The operations that follow are computed in reals, as the released kernel computes them in 32-bit floats.

1399870494.title: qgrp
1399870494.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

286813.title: \text{Cast}
286813.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. The written format holds an element in 16 bits against the 32 of the operand's format, so every value is replaced by the nearest number the written format holds. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

1811877590.title: back
1811877590.description: Counts entries back from the entry named by a position. Distance i_r of entry i_b reads the entry i_r places before it. A distance that reaches before the first entry holds no value.

1970712910.title: pos
1970712910.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

2102340518.title: (\lvert d \rvert \lvert i \rvert)^{-1/2} x
2102340518.description: This map multiplies the weight of every indexer head by 1/64. The released indexer multiplies by one over the square root of the key width, which is 128, and by one over the square root of the head count, which is 32. The model drawn without the omitted mechanisms folds this factor into the weight `w^{I}`. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1000418668.title: \text{IndexSelect}
1000418668.description: Reads the payload at an index that arrives as data. The index is a natural number below the size of the axis it reads along. The operator is broadcast over every other axis, so one entry is read per index.

1783239501.title: \text{TopK}
1783239501.formula: \{p[i_{s|x}]\} = \{i_{C} : s[i_{C}] \text{ is among the } |s|_{512} \text{ largest of } s\}
1783239501.description: Keeps the positions of the largest scores along the axis consumed and hands out no score, because nothing reads a score after the selection. Each result is a natural number, one per slot of the result's axis. A slot with no entry to hold reads the unit.

624478009.title: \text{Cast}
624478009.description: The cast reads a value held in INT64 and writes it in INT32. The written format holds an element in 32 bits against the 64 of the operand's format, so every value is replaced by the nearest number the written format holds. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

523225846.title: \text{Entry Gather}
523225846.description: The gather reads the latents of the selected entries. The compressed entries are read back from every entry and merged onto the queries the way the indexer reads its keys. One latent is read per slot at the distance held by the selection for that slot.

1922804385.title: back
1922804385.description: Counts entries back from the entry named by a position. Distance i_r of entry i_b reads the entry i_r places before it. A distance that reaches before the first entry holds no value.

2028015111.title: pos
2028015111.description: Writes the input at each position to the output at the position given for it by the row of the formula. An output position written by no input position holds the unit of the datatype. An ordinary view reads in the other direction. It takes the output at each position from the input at the position named by its row.

1699955969.title: \text{IndexSelect}
1699955969.description: Reads the payload at an index that arrives as data. The index is a natural number below the size of the axis it reads along. The operator is broadcast over every other axis, so one entry is read per index.

1920636127.title: \text{Concatenation}
1920636127.description: Writes each input onto its own run of the concatenated axis. The second run comes after the first. The size of that axis is therefore the sum of the sizes of the parts. Every other axis is carried through unchanged.

138745809.title: \text{Attention Core}
138745809.description: The attention core computes one head's softmax over the window slots, the selected entries and the learned sink. The two kinds of latent are laid end to end along one slot axis. The query scores against the latent at every slot. The scores are exponentiated. One copy is summed into the denominator together with the exponentiated sink logit. The reciprocal of that sum scales the exponentials contracted against the latents. Every score is multiplied by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model, before it is exponentiated. The scale keeps the spread of the scores the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The sink logit is one learned number per head that lets the head give part of its weight to no slot. The sink logit is exponentiated with no scale.

1400240886.title: \lvert c \rvert^{-1/2} x
1400240886.description: This map multiplies every attention score by one over the square root of the latent width, which is 512 in the released model. A score is a sum over the 512 channels of a latent, so its spread grows with the square root of that width. The scale keeps the spread the same at any width, so the softmax does not put nearly all of its weight on one slot. The model drawn without the omitted mechanisms folds this factor into the query weight. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1928642168.title: z^{-1}
1928642168.description: This map is the reciprocal of a normalising sum. The attention core divides each exponentiated score by the sum over its slots and the sink. The division is written as a product with this reciprocal. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1202406043.title: \text{Cast}
1202406043.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. The written format holds an element in 16 bits against the 32 of the operand's format, so every value is replaced by the nearest number the written format holds. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

1560225213.title: \text{Cast}
1560225213.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. 1255488889.title: \text{Pairs as Complex Numbers}
1255488889.description: Reads every two adjacent channels as one complex number, with the first channel as the real part and the second as the imaginary part. A complex number is a point in a plane. Multiplying the point by a complex number of length one turns it about the origin, so the rotation of a pair is one product.

1053937183.title: \text{Cast}
1053937183.description: The cast reads a value held in BF16 and writes it in FP32. The written format holds an element in 32 bits against the 16 of the operand's format, and holds every number that format holds, so no value changes. The wire on each side of the cast is labelled with its quantisation.

1473337102.title: \text{Complex Numbers as Pairs}
1473337102.formula: y[2 i_{t}] = \mathrm{Re}\, p[i_{t}], \qquad y[2 i_{t} + 1] = \mathrm{Im}\, p[i_{t}]
1473337102.description: Writes every complex number back as two adjacent channels, with the real part first and the imaginary part second. The operation undoes the reading of the channels as pairs.

245496469.title: \text{Cast}
245496469.description: The cast reads a value held in FP32 and writes it in BF16. The written format holds an element in 16 bits against the 32 of the operand's format, so every value is replaced by the nearest number the written format holds. 1320038689.title: \text{Concatenation of the Channels}
1320038689.description: Joins the channels left alone by the rotation and the rotated channels back into one vector. The run left alone comes first and the rotated run comes after it. 226518447.title: grp

The attention cuts the heads into groups for the grouped output projection. The ratio-2 compressor cuts the tokens into entries of two. The pixel unshuffle of the image pathway cuts the rows of the patch grid into cell rows of three and its columns into cell columns of three.

534053567.title: \text{Cast to MXFP8}
534053567.formula: \begin{gathered}a[i_{g}] = \max_{i_{y} \in y} \lvert x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] \rvert \\s[i_{g}] = 2^{\lceil \log_{2} (\max(a[i_{g}],\, 10^{-4}) / 448) \rceil} \\\hat{x}[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] = \mathrm{E4M3}\big(\ulcorner x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] / s[i_{g}] \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}\big)\end{gathered}
534053567.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

1340619162.title: \text{Single-Pass mHC}
1340619162.description: One sublayer runs inside the four-stream residual. The coefficients are predicted from the four streams. The streams are summed into one hidden state under the collapse vector predicted by the previous sublayer. The hidden state is normalised. The body runs on the result. The output vector times the body's result is added to the combine matrix applied to the four streams. The collapse vector predicted here goes to the next sublayer.

1108782479.title: \text{Cast}

1191329690.title: \sigma
1191329690.description: The sigmoid is applied to the collapse vector of a hyper-connection, so the weight of each stream lies between zero and one. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1412742297.title: x + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{hc}}
1412742297.description: This map adds the epsilon of the hyper-connections, `hc_eps` in the released configuration, which is one millionth. The epsilon is added to the collapse vector after the sigmoid and to the combine matrix after the row softmax. Every value is therefore above zero. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

1465286043.title: 2\sigma
1465286043.description: Twice the sigmoid is applied to the output vector of a hyper-connection, so the weight of each stream lies between zero and two. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

The square root of the positive score is taken. The result is the gate of the expert. An elementwise map. Every value x of the input is replaced by the value y the formula gives at it.

483639084.title: \text{TopK}
483639084.formula: y[i_{e}] = s[i_{e}] \text{ where } s[i_{e}] \text{ is among the } |k|_{6} \text{ largest of } s

2013973717.title: \text{Select}

2108917592.title: \tfrac{3}{2}x

Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. 581649965.title: \log_{2} x

2064078036.title: \text{Ceiling}
2064078036.formula: \lceil \cdot \rceil : R[\,] \to R[\,], \qquad \lceil x \rceil = \min \{ n \in \mathbb{Z} : n \geq x \}

1386873758.title: \text{Entry Gather}
1386873758.description: The gather reads the latents of the selected entries. The compressed entries are read back from every entry and merged onto the queries the way the indexer reads its keys. One latent is read per slot at the distance held by the selection for that slot.

363495960.title: back

261113810.title: pos

82065692.title: \text{Cast to MXFP8}
82065692.formula: \begin{gathered}a[i_{g}] = \max_{i_{y} \in y} \lvert x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] \rvert \\s[i_{g}] = 2^{\lceil \log_{2} (\max(a[i_{g}],\, 10^{-4}) / 448) \rceil} \\\hat{x}[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] = \mathrm{E4M3}\big(\ulcorner x[32\, i_{g} + i_{y}] / s[i_{g}] \lrcorner_{-448}^{448}\big)\end{gathered}
82065692.description: The released code runs this rounding kernel in front of every projection whose weight is FP8 or FP4. The channels of a row are cut into groups of 32. The largest magnitude of a group, kept at or above 10^-4, is divided by 448 and rounded up to a power of two, which is the UE8M0 scale of the group. Each channel is divided by the scale, kept between -448 and 448, and rounded to the nearest E4M3 number. The wire after the cast carries the E4M3 element of every channel and the scale of every group. The value denoted by the wire is the element multiplied by the scale. The GEMM reading the wire multiplies its FP32 accumulator by the scale of the operand and by the scale of the weight. The product is therefore of the values written above. A cast to E4M3 with no scale would saturate above 448 and flush to zero below 2^-9.

9.formula: \mathrm{RMSNorm}_{n, m}(x) = x \left(\frac{1}{|n||m|}\sum_{i_{n} \in n,\, i_{m} \in m} x[i_{n}, i_{m}]^{2} + \varepsilon\right)^{-1/2}
9.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

10.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

15.description: The output projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the output vector, one number per stream. A doubled sigmoid keeps the output vector between zero and two. The released code holds the projection as the second n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the second entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the second n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.
