31.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

37.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

40.formula: y[i_{h}, i_{c}] = \sum_{i_{q} \in q} x[i_{q}]\, W_\bold{W^{Qb}}[i_{q}, i_{h}, i_{c}]
40.description: The query up projection maps the normalised query latent to one query of the latent width c for each of the h heads. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

48.description: The table of rotary factors of the two sliding-window layers holds one complex number of length one for every token position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 10000 and no YaRN correction. The released `apply_rotary_emb` multiplies the pairs by the table. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio.

56.description: The window latent projection maps each token's hidden state to one latent of width c. Every head reads that latent as both the key and the value of that token inside the sliding window. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

57.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

64.description: The table of rotary factors of the two sliding-window layers holds one complex number of length one for every token position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 10000 and no YaRN correction. The released `apply_rotary_emb` multiplies the pairs by the table. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio.

124.description: The table of rotary factors of the two sliding-window layers holds one complex number of length one for every token position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 10000 and no YaRN correction. The released `apply_rotary_emb` multiplies the pairs by the table. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio.

136.description: In the first half of the grouped output projection the heads are cut into g groups. Each group has a weight of its own that maps its j heads of width c to a rank of width o. The released model reads this weight at BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. The file holds it in E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

151.formula: \mathrm{RMSNorm}_{n, m}(x) = x \left(\frac{1}{|n||m|}\sum_{i_{n} \in n,\, i_{m} \in m} x[i_{n}, i_{m}]^{2} + \varepsilon\right)^{-1/2}
151.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

152.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

157.description: The output projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the output vector, one number per stream. A doubled sigmoid keeps the output vector between zero and two. The released code holds the projection as the second n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the second entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the second n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. The file holds it in BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

195.description: The gate projection of the routed experts is `w1` of the released expert. The weight holds the projection of every expert, from the residual width m to the expert width f. Its result passes through the sigmoid weighted input before it multiplies the up projection. The released model reads this weight at MXFP4: E2M1, 4 bits, packed 8 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 channels. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

274.description: The value projection of the Engram module of layer 1 reads the same 24 vectors and gives one value of the residual width. Every stream receives that value under its own gate. The released code holds the projection as the last 5120 outputs of `wkv`. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

277.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

278.description: The weight of the Engram gate of layer 1, one learned number for each stream and channel, multiplies the product of the stream and its key before the sum over the channels. The released code holds two arrays, `q_weight` and `k_weight`, and uses only their product. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. The file holds it in BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned array. It reads no input, so its weight is the whole of its result, and the array is read from the tape.

281.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

294.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

295.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

303.description: The combine projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to an n by N matrix. The exponential and the Sinkhorn rounds after the projection make that matrix doubly stochastic. The released code holds the projection as the last n N rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the third entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the last n N entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

320.description: The sink logit is one learned number per head. Its exponential joins the denominator of the head's softmax and carries no value, so a head can give part of its weight to no slot. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned array. It reads no input, so its weight is the whole of its result, and the array is read from the tape.

321.description: The query down projection maps each token's hidden state to the query latent of width q. The attention query and the indexer query are both made from that latent. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

322.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

325.formula: y[i_{h}, i_{c}] = \sum_{i_{q} \in q} x[i_{q}]\, W_\bold{W^{Qb}}[i_{q}, i_{h}, i_{c}]
325.description: The query up projection maps the normalised query latent to one query of the latent width c for each of the h heads. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

333.description: The table of rotary factors of the two sliding-window layers holds one complex number of length one for every token position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 10000 and no YaRN correction. The released `apply_rotary_emb` multiplies the pairs by the table. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio.

341.description: The window latent projection maps each token's hidden state to one latent of width c. Every head reads that latent as both the key and the value of that token inside the sliding window. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

342.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

349.description: The table of rotary factors of the two sliding-window layers holds one complex number of length one for every token position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 10000 and no YaRN correction. The released `apply_rotary_emb` multiplies the pairs by the table. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio.

409.description: The table of rotary factors of the two sliding-window layers holds one complex number of length one for every token position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 10000 and no YaRN correction. The released `apply_rotary_emb` multiplies the pairs by the table. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio.

421.description: In the first half of the grouped output projection the heads are cut into g groups. Each group has a weight of its own that maps its j heads of width c to a rank of width o. The released model reads this weight at BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. The file holds it in E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

436.formula: \mathrm{RMSNorm}_{n, m}(x) = x \left(\frac{1}{|n||m|}\sum_{i_{n} \in n,\, i_{m} \in m} x[i_{n}, i_{m}]^{2} + \varepsilon\right)^{-1/2}
436.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

437.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

442.description: The output projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the output vector, one number per stream. A doubled sigmoid keeps the output vector between zero and two. The released code holds the projection as the second n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the second entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the second n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

445.description: The combine projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to an n by N matrix. The exponential and the Sinkhorn rounds after the projection make that matrix doubly stochastic. The released code holds the projection as the last n N rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the third entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the last n N entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

458.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

463.description: The router scores one token's hidden state against each of the e routed experts. The square root of the softplus of a score is the expert's gate. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. The file holds it in BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

537.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

538.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

543.description: The output projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the output vector, one number per stream. A doubled sigmoid keeps the output vector between zero and two. The released code holds the projection as the second n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the second entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the second n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

559.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

563.description: The query down projection maps each token's hidden state to the query latent of width q. The attention query and the indexer query are both made from that latent. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

564.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

568.formula: y[i_{h}, i_{c}] = \sum_{i_{q} \in q} x[i_{q}]\, W_\bold{W^{Qb}}[i_{q}, i_{h}, i_{c}]
568.description: The query up projection maps the normalised query latent to one query of the latent width c for each of the h heads. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

576.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
576.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

584.description: The window latent projection maps each token's hidden state to one latent of width c. Every head reads that latent as both the key and the value of that token inside the sliding window. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

585.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

592.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
592.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

642.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

643.description: The indexer key projection maps the latent of each compressed entry to one key of width d, read by every indexer head. The released model reads this weight at BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

644.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

651.formula: F[i_{b}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, |a|\, i_{b}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
651.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every index of b and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the token position |a| i times the frequency of the pair, with i the index along b. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

691.description: The indexer query projection maps the query latent to one query of width d for each of the i indexer heads. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

698.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
698.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

741.description: The indexer head weights, `weights_proj` of the released indexer, read one number per indexer head off the token's hidden state. Each head's score is scaled in the combined score by the number read for that head. The released model reads this weight at BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

755.formula: F[i_{b}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, |a|\, i_{b}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
755.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every index of b and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the token position |a| i times the frequency of the pair, with i the index along b. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

821.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
821.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

848.formula: \mathrm{RMSNorm}_{n, m}(x) = x \left(\frac{1}{|n||m|}\sum_{i_{n} \in n,\, i_{m} \in m} x[i_{n}, i_{m}]^{2} + \varepsilon\right)^{-1/2}
848.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

849.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

857.description: The combine projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to an n by N matrix. The exponential and the Sinkhorn rounds after the projection make that matrix doubly stochastic. The released code holds the projection as the last n N rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the third entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the last n N entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

870.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

875.description: The router scores one token's hidden state against each of the e routed experts. The square root of the softplus of a score is the expert's gate. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. The file holds it in BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

880.description: The correction bias of the router, one learned number per expert, is added to a copy of the gates. The experts of a token are chosen from that copy. The gates without the bias weight the experts chosen. The bias therefore balances the load and does not scale a result. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned array. It reads no input, so its weight is the whole of its result, and the array is read from the tape.

892.description: The gate projection of the routed experts is `w1` of the released expert. The weight holds the projection of every expert, from the residual width m to the expert width f. Its result passes through the sigmoid weighted input before it multiplies the up projection. The released model reads this weight at MXFP4: E2M1, 4 bits, packed 8 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 channels. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

949.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

950.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

955.description: The output projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the output vector, one number per stream. A doubled sigmoid keeps the output vector between zero and two. The released code holds the projection as the second n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the second entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the second n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

971.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

976.description: The query down projection maps each token's hidden state to the query latent of width q. The attention query and the indexer query are both made from that latent. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

977.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

980.formula: y[i_{h}, i_{c}] = \sum_{i_{q} \in q} x[i_{q}]\, W_\bold{W^{Qb}}[i_{q}, i_{h}, i_{c}]
980.description: The query up projection maps the normalised query latent to one query of the latent width c for each of the h heads. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

988.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
988.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

996.description: The window latent projection maps each token's hidden state to one latent of width c. Every head reads that latent as both the key and the value of that token inside the sliding window. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

997.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

1004.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
1004.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

1072.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
1072.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

1099.formula: \mathrm{RMSNorm}_{n, m}(x) = x \left(\frac{1}{|n||m|}\sum_{i_{n} \in n,\, i_{m} \in m} x[i_{n}, i_{m}]^{2} + \varepsilon\right)^{-1/2}
1099.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

1100.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1105.description: The output projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the output vector, one number per stream. A doubled sigmoid keeps the output vector between zero and two. The released code holds the projection as the second n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the second entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the second n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1121.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

1126.description: The router scores one token's hidden state against each of the e routed experts. The square root of the softplus of a score is the expert's gate. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. The file holds it in BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1222.description: The value projection of the Engram module of layer 14 reads the same 24 vectors and gives one value of the residual width. Every stream receives that value under its own gate. The released code holds the projection as the last 5120 outputs of `wkv`. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1225.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

1243.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1251.description: The combine projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to an n by N matrix. The exponential and the Sinkhorn rounds after the projection make that matrix doubly stochastic. The released code holds the projection as the last n N rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the third entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the last n N entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1268.description: The query down projection maps each token's hidden state to the query latent of width q. The attention query and the indexer query are both made from that latent. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1269.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

1273.description: The query up projection maps the normalised query latent to one query of the latent width c for each of the h heads. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1281.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
1281.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

1289.description: The window latent projection maps each token's hidden state to one latent of width c. Every head reads that latent as both the key and the value of that token inside the sliding window. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1290.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

1297.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
1297.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

1347.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1349.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

1356.formula: F[i_{b}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, |a|\, i_{b}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
1356.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every index of b and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the token position |a| i times the frequency of the pair, with i the index along b. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

1396.description: The indexer query projection maps the query latent to one query of width d for each of the i indexer heads. The released model reads this weight at E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1403.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
1403.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

1446.description: The indexer head weights, `weights_proj` of the released indexer, read one number per indexer head off the token's hidden state. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

1460.formula: F[i_{b}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, |a|\, i_{b}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
1460.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every index of b and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the token position |a| i times the frequency of the pair, with i the index along b. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.
