2948.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
2948.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

3016.formula: F[i_{x}, i_{t}] = e^{\mathrm{i}\, i_{x}\, \theta'[i_{t}]},\quad \theta'[i_{t}] = \beta^{-i_{t} / |t|}\, (1 - r[i_{t}] + r[i_{t}] / \kappa),\quad r[i_{t}] = \ulcorner (i_{t} - \mathrm{lo}) / (\mathrm{hi} - \mathrm{lo}) \lrcorner
3016.description: The table of rotary factors of every layer that holds compressed entries has one complex number of length one for every position and channel pair. The released `precompute_freqs_cis` computes it with the base 160000 and the YaRN correction, which divides the frequency of the slow channel pairs by 16 and fades the pairs between the ramp ends across. Each pair of channels is one point in the plane, and a rotary embedding turns that point counterclockwise about the origin by an angle that grows with the position. The table holds the turn for every position of x and every pair of t, as a complex number of length one whose angle is the position times the frequency of the pair. Pair 0 has the frequency one and turns fastest, and before YaRN each later pair turns more slowly than the pair before it by one constant ratio. YaRN keeps the frequency of the fastest pairs and divides the frequency of the slowest pairs by its factor, so that a context that many times longer than the trained one turns the slow pairs through angles seen in training.

3028.description: In the first half of the grouped output projection the heads are cut into g groups. Each group has a weight of its own that maps its j heads of width c to a rank of width o. The released model reads this weight at BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. The file holds it in E4M3, 8 bits, packed 4 to a word, with one UE8M0 scale per 32 by 32 block. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

3043.formula: \mathrm{RMSNorm}_{n, m}(x) = x \left(\frac{1}{|n||m|}\sum_{i_{n} \in n,\, i_{m} \in m} x[i_{n}, i_{m}]^{2} + \varepsilon\right)^{-1/2}
3043.description: A root-mean-square normalisation of the released `RMSNorm` class has the epsilon `norm_eps` of the released configuration under the root and a learned gain per channel. The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

3044.description: The collapse projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the collapse vector, one number per stream. A sigmoid keeps the collapse vector between zero and one. The released code holds the projection as the first n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the first entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the first n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

3049.description: The output projection of the hyper-connection maps the n normalised streams of a token to the output vector, one number per stream. A doubled sigmoid keeps the output vector between zero and two. The released code holds the projection as the second n rows of `hc_attn_fn` or `hc_ffn_fn`, times the second entry of `hc_attn_scale`, with the second n entries of `hc_attn_base` as its bias. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. It then adds the bias, one learned value per output position. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

The normalisation applied by DSpark to the projected backbone state is one of these normalisations. The hyper-connection and Engram normalisations have no gain and are written out in primitives instead. Each value divided by the root of the mean of the squares over the normalised axes, with the epsilon of the operator added under the root. The gain, which is one learned weight per position of the normalised axes, multiplies the result where the operator declares one, and the bias is added after it where the operator declares one.

3070.description: The router scores one token's hidden state against each of the e routed experts. The square root of the softplus of a score is the expert's gate. The released model reads this weight at FP32, 32 bits. The file holds it in BF16, 16 bits, packed 2 to a word. A learned linear map. The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.

3075.description: The correction bias of the router, one learned number per expert, is added to a copy of the gates. The experts of a token are chosen from that copy. It reads no input, so its weight is the whole of its result, and the array is read from the tape.

The weight holds one value for every pair of an input position and an output position, and the map contracts the input against the weight over the input positions. The arrays are read from the tape, and they are shared by every position of the axes the map is broadcast over.
